title: Annotatio VI §.VII: is spiritual presence mere imagination? Faith then empty?
pass_a_gloss: Does the most distinguished Author therefore imagine to himself the Spiritual presence of Christ and of his body and blood — by which he is most present in an ineffable mode to his faithful’s souls, both in the Holy Supper and outside it, his flesh their true food nourishing them to eternal life, his blood true drink purging their consciences from dead works to serve the one true GOD — as merely imaginary, void of all reality and truth? Nay, he himself conceives FAITH, by which alone CHRIST is most tightly united to his members and they to CHRIST, as quite jejune and idle!
pass_b_english: So is spiritual presence of Christ, body, and blood — most present to faithful souls in and beyond the Supper, true food and drink unto eternal life — mere imagination void of reality?
Then he empties FAITH itself, the one bond by which Christ and his members are tightly united.
source_text: Ergone Clarissimus Auctor Spiritualem Christi corporísque ejus & sanguinis præsentiam, (quâ is fidelium suorum animabus, cum in Cœna S. tùm extra eam, ineffabili modo præsentissimus est, caro ejus, istarum verus cibus, nutriens eas ad vitam æternam, sanguis ejus verus potus, purgans earum conscientias à pravis operibus ad inseriendum Vero uni DEO) merè imaginariam sibi imaginatur, omnis realitatis & veritatis expertem? Næ ipse FIDEM, per quam unam, CHRISTUS membris suis, & hæc CHRISTO, arctissimè uniuntur, admodum jejunam & otiosam concipit!
notes: Spiritual presence not imaginary; faith not empty.
